questions.stem: In AI / Machine Learning Feature Modelling, what is a feature?
options: A screen in a machine learning application
A measurable variable used as an input to a machine learning model
A column in a dimension table
A rule in a security policy
A version of a trained model
questions.explanation: Features are the measurable variables used as inputs to machine learning models, which Feature Modelling designs, structures and governs.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of Feature Modelling?
options: To let every data scientist build their own version of each metric
To replace dimensional modelling in the warehouse
To provide a standardised, governed framework so features are defined once and reused consistently
To store raw transactional data directly in ML algorithms
To eliminate the need for data stewards
questions.explanation: Feature Modelling ensures features are defined once, documented clearly and reused consistently rather than being recreated in slightly different versions by each data scientist.

options: A marketplace where third-party models are sold
A backup of a data warehouse
A dashboard showing model accuracy
A centralised repository where engineered features are stored, versioned and made available for training and inference
A list of security roles for data scientists
questions.explanation: The Feature Store is a centralised repository that stores and versions engineered features so they can be reused consistently across models.

questions.stem: Which of the following must a Feature Definition include?
options: A clear name, calculation logic, data sources, refresh frequency and ownership
The model's hyperparameters
The GPU used for training
A star schema diagram
The list of end users of the model
questions.explanation: Each feature must have a clear name, calculation logic, data sources, refresh frequency and ownership.

questions.stem: How is Repayment_DelinquencyRate defined in the banking example from I Am Datapedia!?
options: The number of prior loans a customer has taken
The percentage of approvals by each officer over six months
The customer's credit score from the bureau
The ratio of late repayments over the past 12 months
The average loan amount per branch
questions.explanation: Repayment_DelinquencyRate is defined as the ratio or proportion of late repayments over the past 12 months.

questions.stem: Which feature in the loan approval example is sourced from credit bureau data and refreshed monthly?
options: Loan_HistoryCount
Officer_ApprovalRate
Customer_CreditScore
Repayment_DelinquencyRate
Customer_IncomeStability
questions.explanation: Customer_CreditScore is sourced from credit bureau data and refreshed monthly, and is flagged as sensitive.

questions.stem: How does Feature Modelling differ from dimensional modelling and metadata modelling?
options: It is focused on analytical reporting
It describes data assets in general
It defines physical storage formats
It is only used for unstructured data
It is explicitly model-input-centric, sitting between data engineering and ML operations
questions.explanation: Dimensional modelling serves reporting and metadata modelling describes assets, whereas Feature Modelling is explicitly centred on machine learning model inputs.

questions.stem: Why do data scientists retrieve features from the Feature Store rather than recalculating them?
options: To ensure consistency between training and production environments and support explainable AI
Because recalculation is forbidden by GDPR
Because the Feature Store is faster than any database
To avoid paying for compute
Because raw data is never stored anywhere else
questions.explanation: Retrieving features from the Feature Store keeps training and production consistent and supports explainability requirements.

questions.stem: Which is described as a drawback of a governed feature catalogue?
options: It increases duplication of features
Excessive governance can slow experimentation in early-stage innovation
It makes models less explainable
It weakens regulatory compliance
It prevents reuse across models
questions.explanation: Maintaining a governed catalogue requires discipline, and excessive governance can slow experimentation, especially early on.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named as a use case that could reuse the same engineered features?
options: Risk scoring
Fraud detection
Churn prediction
Payroll processing
Loan approval
questions.explanation: Features are reused across models such as risk scoring, fraud detection, churn prediction and the loan approval pipeline; payroll processing is not mentioned.
